governanceNotes: Deliberate deferral, not an authored suggestion: common peroneal (fibular) neuropathy IS the clinical identity whose defining presentation is foot drop with dorsiflexion weakness and sensory loss in the peroneal distribution, so an edge from this identity to any catalog outcome expressing foot drop, dorsiflexion weakness, or peroneal sensory deficit would restate the diagnostic presentation (the ME-41 phenotype-identity barrier).

The natural downstream candidates lack catalog identities (falls and trip-related injury, gait deviation, ankle-foot-orthosis dependence, chronic paresthesia), and the remaining catalog neuropathy targets are sibling identities whose edges would run sideways rather than downstream; the surgical-decompression and tendon-transfer literature is treatment-class rather than natural-history evidence, so no defensible target identity exists.
